title: How to Prevent Motorbike Theft in Hanoi: Parking, Locks and Bag Safety
meta_description: How motorbike thieves operate in Hanoi, which locks and parking habits Hanoi police recommend, how to keep bags and phones safe from snatching, and what to do if your rental bike is stolen.
h1: How to Prevent Motorbike Theft in Hanoi
body_markdown:
A rented motorbike is one of the most valuable things a traveller has in Hanoi, and it is also an easy target. Most thefts are not dramatic: a bike left without the steering lock in a quiet lane, a scooter parked overnight outside a guesthouse, a bag on the shoulder of a pedestrian at the kerb. This guide collects the advice Hanoi police officers give residents, explains which locks and parking habits make a difference, how to keep bags and phones out of reach of snatch thieves, and what to do if the bike disappears anyway. For the wider picture on safe riding, see our topic page on [safer riding and breakdown support](/en/topics/riding-safety-and-support/).

## How motorbike thieves operate

In a December 2024 report, Lieutenant Colonel Nguyễn Đức Hưng, deputy chief of the Hàng Trống ward police in the Old Quarter, described thieves who study their targets in advance: daily routines, entrances and exits, and the position of cameras and alarms ([Diễn đàn Doanh nghiệp, 20 December 2024](https://diendandoanhnghiep.vn/canh-bao-nan-trom-cap-xe-may-dip-cuoi-nam-va-cach-phong-tranh-hieu-qua-10147654.html)). The same report describes a pair who rented a guesthouse room in Cầu Giấy, watched the evening coming and going in areas with many rented rooms, and took bikes whose steering lock had not been engaged. They hid the bikes on vacant land before selling them, and they also carried tools to break locks.

The lesson for renters is simple. Thieves look for the easiest bike in a row, not for a particular model. A bike with its steering locked, a second lock on the wheel and the key in your pocket is more trouble than the one next to it.

## Locks that make a difference

The police advice in the same report is practical ([Diễn đàn Doanh nghiệp](https://diendandoanhnghiep.vn/canh-bao-nan-trom-cap-xe-may-dip-cuoi-nam-va-cach-phong-tranh-hieu-qua-10147654.html)):

- **Lock the steering and the fork** whenever you leave the bike outdoors or in a quiet place, and take the key with you.
- **Add a second lock**: a wheel lock, a disc-brake lock, an anti-theft lock or a tracking device.
- **Choose good-quality locks** with high security, and do not rely on a cheap padlock alone.
- **Check before you walk away** that the engine is off and both locks have engaged.

Ask the rental shop whether the bike comes with a disc lock or chain. If it does, note on the pickup form that you received it, and photograph the keys you were given. Our [pickup checklist](/en/checklist/) helps you record the bike's condition and accessories at handover.

## Where to leave the bike

The safest place is a guarded parking point with an attendant, where you receive a numbered ticket. The police advice is to use car parks with guards or attendants, or at least well-lit places with good visibility, and to remember the ticket number or photograph the number plate when you use a public car park ([Diễn đàn Doanh nghiệp](https://diendandoanhnghiep.vn/canh-bao-nan-trom-cap-xe-may-dip-cuoi-nam-va-cach-phong-tranh-hieu-qua-10147654.html)).

At night, ask your accommodation where to put the bike. Many guesthouses bring scooters indoors or into a courtyard after dark, or have an arrangement with a nearby parking point. A rental bike left on the pavement overnight is exactly what the thieves in the report were looking for. The fee for guarded parking is small next to the value of the bike; our guide to [costs beyond the rental fee](/en/guides/costs-beyond-the-rental-fee/) shows how parking fits into the budget.

## Bags and phones: preventing snatch theft

Theft does not only target parked bikes. Hanoi police have warned that snatch thieves on motorbikes, often with the number plate removed or replaced by a fake one, follow and target people who leave an opening, such as a bag carried on the shoulder ([Báo Pháp luật, 31 October 2018](https://baophapluat.vn/cong-an-khuyen-cao-5-bien-phap-chong-cuop-giat-tren-duong-ha-noi-post290083.html)). The police recommend five measures ([Báo Pháp luật](https://baophapluat.vn/cong-an-khuyen-cao-5-bien-phap-chong-cuop-giat-tren-duong-ha-noi-post290083.html)):

1. Wear little jewellery when you go out.
2. Watch your surroundings and keep away from suspicious people.
3. Do not give strangers a lift on your bike.
4. Stay calm if you are robbed and call out for help from people nearby.
5. Remember the offender's features so that you can report them.

For riders, a few habits follow from this. Carry bags across your body and in front of you, not on the shoulder facing the traffic. Keep the phone in a zipped pocket when you are not navigating, and do not stand at the kerb holding it while you wait for a ride. On the bike, put bags in the under-seat compartment or wear them, rather than hanging them on the front hook where a passing hand can reach them.

## Papers and valuables

Never leave the vehicle registration card, your passport or cash in the bike. The registration card belongs with you while you ride, as our guide on [which papers to carry](/en/guides/papers-to-carry-registration-card/) explains, and a stolen bike with its papers inside is easier to sell. If a rental shop asks to keep your passport as a deposit, read our guide on [leaving your passport as a rental deposit](/en/guides/passport-as-rental-deposit/) first.

## What insurance does and does not cover

The compulsory civil liability insurance every motorbike must carry pays for damage to third parties and for injuries to passengers caused by the vehicle ([Decree 67/2023/NĐ-CP, Article 7](https://thuvienphapluat.vn/van-ban/Bao-hiem/Nghi-dinh-67-2023-ND-CP-bao-hiem-bat-buoc-trach-nhiem-dan-su-cua-chu-xe-co-gioi-578283.aspx)). It does not pay for the bike itself, so it is no help if the rental bike is stolen. Our guide to [compulsory motorbike insurance in Vietnam](/en/guides/compulsory-motorbike-insurance-in-vietnam/) explains what the policy covers, and our guide on [travel insurance for riding a motorbike](/en/guides/travel-insurance-motorbike-vietnam/) explains what to check in your own policy.

## If the bike is stolen

- **Call the rental shop at once.** They know the bike's registration details and can help with the police report.
- **Report it to the police.** Go to the police of the ward where it happened, or call the police emergency number [113](https://thuvienphapluat.vn/hoi-dap-phap-luat/111-113-114-115-la-so-dien-thoai-gi-138013545.html) if you need urgent help. Bring your passport, the rental contract and any photos of the bike and parking ticket.
- **Ask for written confirmation** of your report. Your insurer and the rental shop will both ask for it.
- **Check your rental contract.** Who pays for a stolen bike depends on what you signed, so read the theft clause and keep all receipts.

## In short

Thieves pick the easiest bike, so lock the steering and the fork, add a disc or wheel lock and take the key ([Diễn đàn Doanh nghiệp](https://diendandoanhnghiep.vn/canh-bao-nan-trom-cap-xe-may-dip-cuoi-nam-va-cach-phong-tranh-hieu-qua-10147654.html)). Use guarded parking with a ticket, especially at night, and keep bags across your body and phones out of sight at the kerb, as Hanoi police advise ([Báo Pháp luật](https://baophapluat.vn/cong-an-khuyen-cao-5-bien-phap-chong-cuop-giat-tren-duong-ha-noi-post290083.html)). Compulsory insurance does not cover the bike itself ([Decree 67/2023/NĐ-CP](https://thuvienphapluat.vn/van-ban/Bao-hiem/Nghi-dinh-67-2023-ND-CP-bao-hiem-bat-buoc-trach-nhiem-dan-su-cua-chu-xe-co-gioi-578283.aspx)), so prevention is worth the effort.
